title: IPv6 DHCPv6 / DNS Takeover (mitm6)
description: Windows hosts prefer IPv6 and request configuration via DHCPv6 by default, even on IPv4-only networks. An attacker can respond as a rogue DHCPv6 server and advertise themselves as the DNS server, then intercept and relay authentication (for example to LDAP or to AD CS), enabling credential capture and potential privilege escalation.
businessImpact: High --- successful attacks can capture and relay authentication to internal services, enabling account compromise and escalation toward domain control.
remediation:
- Disable IPv6 where it is not used, or filter rogue DHCPv6 with RA Guard / DHCPv6 Guard on switches.
- Require LDAP signing/channel binding and SMB signing to prevent relay.
- Enable Extended Protection for Authentication on relay targets such as AD CS.
- Monitor for rogue DHCPv6/RA traffic on network segments.
